narrative:
The model estimates a 66% chance that you will leave your current job. Because of this, the organization has decided to deny your promotion, as they are concerned about investing in someone likely to depart soon.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. First, your total years of experience across all jobs had the strongest influence, pulling the prediction toward you staying. With only 1-5 years of overall experience, you fall into the most common group among employees the model expects to remain, which normally signals stability. However, this positive signal was outweighed by the next two factors.

Having received other job offers while at your current employer was the second most important driver and strongly pushed the prediction toward leaving. The model sees external opportunities as a clear sign you may depart. Finally, your sense of low job stability also contributed toward predicting you will leave. Feeling that your position is not secure makes it more likely you will look elsewhere, even though most employees the model predicts will stay report feeling secure.

Taken together, your external opportunities and lack of felt stability were more powerful than your relatively short but common experience level. The organization should discuss with you how to strengthen your sense of security and explore whether those outside offers can be matched internally. You may want to reflect on what would make you feel more committed to staying long-term. (248 words)
